writeup: TIC 349252594 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 14.866878 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.22 percent, while a secondary eclipse was not detected. The signal carries a detection significance of 16.4 in the Box Least Squares periodogram, with pixel-level difference imaging confirming a peak signal-to-noise of 13.9, though the centroid offset of 20.1 arcseconds from the target warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. However, a data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth (z-score 4.95), suggesting the true period may be double the initial measurement; the corrected period of 14.866878 days accounts for this effect.
